title: 3 BOUND VOLUMES EXAMINER NEWSP...
description: 3 BOUND VOLUMES EXAMINER NEWSPAPER FROM 1930 AND 1962
findings: Three bound volumes of The Examiner (Launceston daily newspaper). Spine labels read: 'EXAMINER JULY-SEPT 1930' (cloth, gilt on red label); second cloth volume label largely illegible, appears 'EXAMINER ... 193?' (likely another 1930 quarter, could not read months); brown half-leather volume '"THE EXAMINER" NOV-DEC 1962'. Interior photos show full-page 1962 Launceston advertisements: Commer 15 cwt van (D.L. Hollis Motors, Haig whisky ad), J.R. Green's Green Door Dulux paint sale (114 Charles Street, Launceston), Tasmanian Fishing Championships Swansea prize page (Holden station sedan, Philips TV). Original bound file copies, Tasmaniana local history interest.
condition: 1930 cloth volumes heavily worn, spines split and frayed, boards scuffed and stained; 1962 volume sound with rubbed leather. Paper browned, pages appear intact in photos. Very large and heavy.
reason: Original bound Launceston Examiner volumes (1930 and 1962), Tasmanian local history with niche collector and library interest.
marks_read: Spine labels: EXAMINER JULY-SEPT 1930; EXAMINER [illegible] 193?; THE EXAMINER NOV-DEC 1962
identification: Three original bound file volumes of The Examiner newspaper, Launceston Tasmania: July-Sept 1930, one further volume c.1930 (label illegible), Nov-Dec 1962.

title: FOLIO OF FRENCH ENGRAVINGS ETC
findings: Paper wrapper folio with cover title 'ETUDES de A. CALAME' (Alexandre Calame, Swiss landscape artist 1810-1864), publisher imprint at foot of cover too small to read. Two loose tinted lithograph landscape studies (rocky gorge with boulders, rocky outcrop with cave and reclining figure), with printed captions and printer lines at foot, too small to read; one appears signed in the stone 'A. Calame'. Also: an etching of a gnarled tree with a faint pencil inscription below the plate (illegible, possibly a dedication and artist signature); a large Victorian architectural print of a multi-storey corner building with flag and royal coat of arms below the image (London street scene, title not legible, possibly a commercial building advertisement print); and a copy of The Mercury (Hobart) with headline 'ANOTHER "WORLD" WATER MAY BE IN SOIL', 'Roo hops mark conquest', 'Luna 15 into another day', i.e. Apollo 11 moon landing coverage, July 1969.
condition: Wrapper worn, edges chipped and spine rubbed; lithographs with foxing and toning to margins; architectural print on blue mount with stained, chipped edges; Mercury newspaper toned and creased.
reason: 19th-century Alexandre Calame lithograph studies folio plus extra prints and an Apollo 11 Mercury, under-described as 'French engravings'.
marks_read: Cover: ETUDES de A. CALAME; signature in stone A. Calame (one plate); The Mercury masthead; royal arms under building print
identification: Alexandre Calame, 'Etudes' lithograph landscape studies folio in original wrappers, c.1840s-1850s, number of plates uncertain; with a pencil-inscribed tree etching, a Victorian London building print and The Mercury Hobart July 1969 Apollo 11 issue.
